beats: Hook: EAGLE does not guess the model's next word; it guesses what the model is thinking just before it speaks (line_eagle_thought_vs_word, the cover).
Three ways to draft (slide 14): a separate small model (the intern), parallel heads (Medusa's parrots), one autoregressive head on the features (the eagle) (line_eagle_three_helpers).

The trade-off (slide 15): speedup = alpha x T_verify(1) / (M x T_draft + T_verify(M)); a heavier drafter pays if more words are accepted per check; the drafter is one layer next to the whole model (line_eagle_one_layer_cake).

EAGLE-1 (slides 16-17): one decoder layer reads the big model's hidden feature plus the last word, predicts the next feature, and the big model's own frozen output head turns it into a word (line_eagle_reads_thought); a static tree.

EAGLE-2 (slides 18-20): a dynamic tree, wide where unsure ("10+2" may go on with + or =, line_eagle_chalkboard_pause with the sum written by pen), deep where sure (line_eagle_scout_paths); acceptance mostly 3-5 tokens.
Temperature (slide 20): low temperature is easier to guess (reuse line_temp_knob).

EAGLE-3 (slides 21-23): fuse features from low, middle and high layers (line_eagle_three_bubbles), drop the feature loss, and practise on its own drafts instead of always being handed the right answer ("training-time test": line_eagle_leash_practice vs line_eagle_solo_course).
It now keeps improving with more data, 1B to 50B training tokens (line_eagle_book_feast).
In practice (slides 24-25): a flag in vLLM / SGLang (reuse line_switch_dimmer); Yggdrasil makes dynamic trees hardware-friendly (line_draft_gardener from L08-02 if it is in the library).
